MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MAY 4, 2020

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR CARMAN at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CARMAN led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioner’s Present:  Zigrang, Medawar, Yoo, Schachter, Scott, Edler, Carman

  Staff Member’s Present:  David Wahba, Community Development and Public Works Director
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES, MARCH 2, 2020

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 2, 2020.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  Planning Commission will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read
  by title only.

  COMMISSIONER SCACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so moved.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  NONE

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-200099; LOCATION: 27 ROLLINGWOOD DRIVE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: KEITH JOHNSON, PRITZKAT & JOHNSON
  ARCHITECTS; A Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-200100) for a one-story
  addition to a single-story residence and garage. A Minor Deviation (MD-200101) is required
  to decrease the front yard area by less than 10% and for the encroachment of the proposed
  addition in the required front yard which does not project closer to the property line than the
  forwardmost building line. A Variance (V-200102) is requested to decrease the side yard
  by more than 10%.

  Associate Planner Thom provided a presentation to the Planning Commission with a summary of
  the staff report for Planning Application No. PA-200099. Since this staff report was prepared and
  the time of this meeting, the neighbor and the applicant have agreed that the proposed roof height
  be lowered to 205.48”.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission: open the
  public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and, adopt
  Resolution No. 20-200099.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, MAY 4, 2020  1
   COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked if this property is zoned for a two-story building. Associate
  Planner Thom stated that a two-story is not prohibited, however, due to the view corridor it needs
  to be evaluated for neighborhood compatibility.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that in the photograph taken from one of the windows, there is a
  vehicle regularly parked there, which blocks more of the view than the original roof height.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  Keith Johnson, Pritzkat & Johnson Architects stated that when the plans were drawn up for this
  project, typical pitches and plate heights were used. However, when the silhouette went up,
  feedback was received from the neighbors concerning view blockage issues. The plans were
  revised to lower the height and his clients requested to have the height lowered another 7 1/2” to
  gain the approval from their neighbors.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked for the height of the original and the revised plate height and roof
  pitch.

  Mr. Johnson stated that the original plate height on the family room in the back was 7’-6” and 3:12
  pitch. In order to lower the height, the additional 7 ½”, the plate height will be 7’-6” in the laundry
  room and the plate height at the back will be 8’-4” to accommodate high windows. The roof pitch
  will be 2.25:12.

  Mr. Jamie Graupner, 24 Rollingwood, stated that he submitted an e-mail on Friday (May 1, 2020)
  regarding the lowering of the roof height by an additional 7 ½” and stated that he appreciates that
  it has been included.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG made motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG commented that the architect did a good job with the design and
  would have agreed to approve it at the original plate height and encouraged approval of the project.

  The Planning Commissioners were all in agreement with COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG’S comment.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 20-200099, WITH THE CONDITION THAT THE RIDGE
  HEIGHT BE LOWERED 7 ½” AS DISCUSSED IN THIS MEETING.

  AYES: Zigrang, Medawar, Yoo, Schachter, Scott, Edler, Carman
  NOES:
  ABSENT:
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No.
  PA-200099, a resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates granting a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination to construct one-story addition to a single-story
  residence. Minor Deviations decrease the front yard setback by less than 10% and for the
  encroachment of the proposed addition into the required front yard which does not project closer
  to the property line than the forwardmost building line and a Variance to decrease the side yard
  setback by more than 10% with the added condition that the ridge height be lowered by an
  additional 7 ½” for 27 Rollingwood Drive. The decision of the Planning Commission is final unless
  an appeal is filed by any person or the City Council by its own motion within the next 20 days. The
  appeal period will end on May 25, 2020 at which time the applicant may submit their plans to the
  Planning Department for zone clearance and subsequently submit their plans to Building and
  Safety for plan check.

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  NONE

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, MAY 4, 2020  2
   10.  MANAGER’S ITEMS

  A.  RHE COVID-19 UPDATE

  Planning Manager Naughton provided the Planning Commission with an update on how the City
  has continued to provided City Services and have moved operations mostly online. Development
  applications and building permits have continued to be issued and staff has been working with LA
  County Building and Safety and Willdan Engineering to make sure that there is continuity in the
  workflow and construction can proceed.

  Planning Manager Naughton encourage the Planning Commissioner’s to visit the City’s website
  which has a comprehensive COVID-19 section where LA County Public Health Press Releases
  are posted. The Community Services Department has done a great job putting together a Virtual
  Recreation page and includes challenges – this week’s challenge is a 10,000 steps challenge.

  The page also has extensive resources for senior, mental health, volunteer opportunities, public
  safety, among other resources. The City has partnered with other cities on the hill to provide a
  comprehensive guide on resources. Cameron Hall, Code Compliance Officer has worked with the
  other cities to put together a list of restaurants open for take-out or food delivery.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the current stay at home order is in effect through May 15.

  Planning Manger Naughton noted that a typo in the urgency ADU ordinance Exhibit A was not
  corrected, but will be corrected in the regular ordinance Exhibit A, which will go before Council for
  second reading and adoption on May 12.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the consultant selection for the Sustainability Element has
  been completed. This is in partnership with SCAG and the City will be preparing a stand-alone
  Sustainability Element as part of the comprehensive General Plan Update.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that HCD has confirmed that the City has been awarded a
  $160K in SB2 planning grant funds, of which, $60K will go towards creating an ADU program and
  $100K will go towards long range efforts.

  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, APRIL 28, 2020

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, APRIL 14, 2020

  C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11A THROUGH 11C

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CARMAN adjourned the meeting at 7:31 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Bridget Carman, Chair
